Gateway 3: When Commercial Is Ready to Share Its Brain

The Build OrderPart 13

By lowob · 26 August 2026 · 10-minute read · Strategy

Gateway 3 is the point at which the commercial record is extended to delivery, finance and people. It should be passed on evidence, not ambition: one decision class recorded for at least two quarters, outcomes written back, value reported in money, permissions holding, an export tested, and a named owner in the next function asking for the record. Delivery comes first because it inherits the client from sales. Finance comes second because it already audits the dollar figures from Gateway 2. People decisions come last, because hiring, promotion and performance carry legal duties that commercial decisions do not, including EU AI Act high-risk obligations for employment systems from 2 December 2027. At each step the owner changes, the outcome lag lengthens and the ceiling on autonomy drops.

The previous two gateways tested the commercial build from inside: Gateway 1 asked whether every outbound action has a named approver, and Gateway 2 asked whether every recorded decision carries a value and an outcome. Gateway 3 asks a different question. Is the commercial record good enough that another function should build on it, rather than start its own?

That question matters because the alternative is common. Each function buys its own assistant and its own connectors, records decisions in its own way, and the firm ends up with four partial brains that cannot read each other. IBM's 2025 CEO study found half of CEOs saying the pace of recent investment had left them with disconnected, piecemeal technology. Extending one working record is how a firm avoids building four.

Why the brain should not spread early

There are two ways to fail at this gateway: too early and never. Too early is the more expensive.

The evidence on scaling is thin because so few firms have done it. McKinsey's 2025 State of AI survey of 1,993 participants found 23% scaling an agentic system somewhere in the enterprise, but no more than 10% reporting scaling agents in any single business function. IBM found only 16% of AI initiatives scaled enterprise-wide. A firm whose commercial record is still unreliable will export the unreliability: missing reasons, unwritten outcomes, inconsistent definitions. A second function inheriting that will conclude the record does not work, and will be right.

Our scale guide, The scale ladder, makes the general version of this point: build the layer the next stage will break, not one two stages ahead. Gateway 3 is that rule applied to functions instead of headcount.

The six tests

Each test has a yes or no answer. All six should be yes before the record extends.

TestEvidence that it passesWhy it matters for the next function
A class recorded for two quartersRecords exist for every decision in the class, not a sampleThe next function needs a working template, not a pilot
Outcomes written back on timeAt least four in five records have outcomes by the check dateProves the habit survives after launch enthusiasm
Value reported in moneyFinance has accepted at least one quarterly money reportThe next function's sponsor will ask the same renewal question
Permissions holdingPermission review done, no open leakage incident, account scoping in placeDelivery, finance and HR data are more sensitive than sales data
Export testedA full export of records and history reloaded elsewhereShared records raise the cost of a lock-in mistake
A pull, not a pushA named owner in the next function has asked for accessRecords spread by mandate are filled in to satisfy a review

The last test is the one we weight most. When a delivery lead starts asking for the pursue-or-pass record before a project kick-off, or a finance director asks to see discount reasons before approving terms, the record has become useful outside its home. If nobody asks, extending it is a mandate, and Part 9 made the point that records filled in to satisfy a review are worse than no records, because they look like evidence and are not.

Delivery: the record follows the client

Delivery is the natural second function because it inherits the client from sales. Every promise made in the pitch becomes a constraint on the work, and most of the costly misunderstandings in a services or project business happen at that handover.

What changes. The decision classes shift from winning work to running it: scope changes, staffing choices, write-offs of time, and escalations. The owner moves from the head of sales to delivery leads. The outcome lag lengthens, from a sales cycle to the length of a project or a renewal. And the context becomes more confidential, because delivery holds the client's own data and problems as well as the firm's view of the client.

The first shared class. The sale-to-delivery handover. A short record at the moment a deal closes: what was promised, what was priced in and what was not, the client's stated success measure, and the discount or concession granted and why. The delivery lead reads it before kick-off; the outcome (project margin, scope disputes, renewal) is written back to the original commercial decisions. That closes a loop sales has never had: whether the way a deal was won made it profitable to deliver.

The dial. Agents can prepare kick-off briefs and flag scope drift against the handover record. Anything that reaches the client still passes Gateway 1.

Finance: the dollar figure gets a co-owner

Finance is already involved by Gateway 3. It signed off the value-at-stake definitions at Gateway 2 and reviews the quarterly money report. Extending the record turns finance from auditor of the commercial record into a contributor to it.

Finance teams are cautious adopters, with reason. Gartner's 2025 survey of 183 finance leaders found 59% using AI in the finance function, up only slightly from 58% in 2024, with knowledge management (49%), accounts payable automation (37%) and anomaly detection (34%) as the leading uses. Weak data quality was the largest barrier, and 91% initially reported low or moderate impact. A finance team that has watched the commercial record produce accepted money reports has evidence that most of those respondents lacked.

What changes. Decision classes such as credit terms for new clients, payment-term exceptions, write-offs and collections priority. These sit inside the firm's financial controls, so segregation of duties applies: the person who records a payment-term exception should not be the one who approves it. The record becomes evidence for auditors, which raises the standard for status and supersession fields (Supersede, never overwrite).

The dial. Agents prepare and reconcile; they do not approve. A collections agent can draft a prioritised list with reasons. A person decides who is chased.

People: the step that changes the legal footing

People decisions pass every test of frequency and consequence, and they are the last function the record should reach. The reason is law, not technology.

RegimeWhat it requiresStatus in 2026
EU AI Act, Annex III (employment)Risk management, data governance, logging and human oversight for AI used in recruitment, promotion, termination, task allocation and performance monitoringUnder the Digital Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since 27 July 2026), applies from 2 December 2027
NYC Local Law 144Bias audit within a year before using an automated employment decision tool, a public summary, and notice to candidatesEnforced since July 2023
UK GDPR, Article 22C, as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025For solely automated significant decisions: information, a chance to make representations, meaningful human review and a way to contestICO guidance in draft, updated March 2026

The ICO's draft guidance is direct about the human review: it "cannot be tokenistic", and the reviewer must have authority to change the outcome. That rules out the pattern of an agent ranking candidates and a person approving the list.

Enforcement has been patchy. New York State's Comptroller found in December 2025 that the city's consumer agency had received only two complaints under Local Law 144 in two years and, in compliance reviews of 32 companies, had found one instance of non-compliance where the auditors identified at least 17 potential instances. Patchy enforcement is not a reason to build carelessly. It is a reason to expect enforcement to tighten.

What changes. The owner is HR, with legal involved. The sensitivity is the highest in the firm. The outcome lag is longest: a hire is graded over a year or more. The dial. Record people decisions, with reasons, so the firm can explain them. Let agents answer questions and draft, at most. No agent ranks, screens or scores people at this stage of the build.

Each function the record reaches brings a new owner, a longer wait for outcomes and a lower ceiling on what agents may do alone.

What changes at each step

FunctionFirst shared decision classNew ownerOutcome lagMain riskAutonomy ceiling
CommercialDiscount exceptions, pursue or passHead of salesA sales cycleReview fatigueAct with approval
DeliverySale-to-delivery handoverDelivery leadsA project or renewalClient confidentialityDraft
FinancePayment-term exceptions, write-offsFinance directorA quarter to a yearSegregation of dutiesDraft and reconcile
PeopleHiring and promotion reasonsHR, with legalA year or moreEmployment law and biasAnswer and draft

The order bends where the business does. In a firm where delivery and sales are the same people, as in many small consultancies, delivery is not a separate extension; it is part of the commercial record from the start. In a regulated lender, finance controls may arrive with the first commercial record, as Part 10 found.

Gateway 3 is also not passed once. In The transitions that break the brain we listed the moments when firms lose their reasoning: a reorganisation that orphans record ownership, an acquisition that brings a second set of definitions, a platform migration that drops supersession links. Any of these should send the firm back through the six tests before the record extends further.

Illustrative example: the handover record that delivery asked for
Decision
Extend the commercial record to delivery with one shared class, the sale-to-delivery handover, after two quarters of discount and pursue-or-pass records.
Reason and owner
Delivery leads had begun asking sellers for discount reasons before kick-offs, after two projects ran at a loss on concessions nobody had passed on. Owned by the head of delivery, with the head of sales as co-owner.
What changed
Every closed deal now carries a handover record; project margin is written back to the original pursue-or-pass and discount records. Finance and people extensions were deferred to the following year.

Illustrative: a composite of a mid-size consultancy, built from patterns across engagements.

lowob takeaways

  • Extend on evidence, not ambition. Six tests; all should be yes.
  • Wait for the pull. The best signal is a named owner in another function asking for the record.
  • Delivery, then finance, then people. Each step lengthens the outcome lag and lowers the autonomy ceiling.
  • People decisions change the law that applies. Record them; do not automate them.
  • Re-test after every transition. Reorganisations, acquisitions and migrations reset the gateway.
Gateway card

Gateway 3: before the record leaves the commercial line

  • One commercial decision class recorded in full for two quarters
  • Outcomes written back by the check date on at least four in five records
  • At least one quarterly money report accepted by finance
  • Permission review complete and account scoping in place
  • Export of records and history tested by reloading it elsewhere
  • A named owner in the receiving function who has asked for access
  • For people decisions: legal review of the applicable employment and data protection rules

Common questions

When should AI be extended beyond sales and marketing?

When the commercial build is working on evidence: decisions recorded with outcomes for two quarters, value reported in money, permissions holding, an export tested, and a named owner in the next function asking for access.

Is AI used in hiring regulated?

Yes. NYC Local Law 144 requires bias audits for automated employment decision tools, UK GDPR requires safeguards for solely automated significant decisions, and EU AI Act obligations for employment systems apply from 2 December 2027 under the Digital Omnibus.

How should finance teams use AI decision records?

To record and reconcile decisions such as payment-term exceptions and write-offs, with segregation of duties preserved. Agents prepare and reconcile; people approve.

What is the first decision to share between sales and delivery?

The sale-to-delivery handover: what was promised, what was priced in, the client's success measure and any concession granted, with project margin written back to the original commercial decisions.

Next move

Ask your delivery lead and your finance director one question each: which commercial decision would you most like to see the reason for? If neither has an answer, the record is not ready to travel yet.
